request: What impact did passing Obamacare have on the federal budget?

reply.reply:
**The ACA paired spending with Medicare savings: authorized discretionary programs could receive almost $100 billion over FY2012-FY2021 if fully funded; two Medicare provisions were estimated to save $25 billion and close to $11 billion over 10 years.**

- CBO estimated almost $100 billion in appropriations over FY2012-FY2021 if ACA-authorized discretionary grant programs were fully funded, but actual funding fell well below that estimate. (R41390, PDF p. 2)
- CBO estimated that the Medicare premium freeze provision would save $25 billion over 10 years and higher premiums for high-income Part D enrollees would save close to $11 billion over 10 years. (R41196, PDF p. 19)

Not yet covered: The reports checked do not give the ACA’s overall net federal budget or deficit effect; these are selected spending and savings components.; The nearly $100 billion estimate assumed full funding; actual discretionary funding was well below it.
reply.reasoning: The evidence shows both spending and savings but does not establish a single net budget effect for the law. The spending estimate was conditional, while the Medicare savings apply to specific provisions.
